# CLAUDE.md

Guidance for Claude Code (claude.ai/code) working with this repo.

## Project Overview

Botlands = 2D game built with LÖVE 2D (v11.4) and Lua 5.1. Composition-based entity system — entities assembled from reusable component functions.

## Commands

```bash
make run            # Run the game (love .)
make test           # Run all tests (spec then unit)
busted path/to/file_test.lua  # Run a single test file
```

Formatting (`stylua`) and linting (`luacheck`) run auto via PostToolUse hooks on every `.lua` edit — don't run manually. `make check` for CI/manual only.

## Prerequisites

Requires: [LÖVE 2D](https://love2d.org/), luarocks packages `busted`, `luacheck`, `stylua`

## Architecture

### Entity Composition System

Entities = plain tables built by composing component functions. Components = higher-order functions returning mutator function:

```lua
local function health(config)
  return function(entity)
    entity.hp = config.max_hp
    local base_update = entity.update
    function entity.update(delta_time)
      if base_update then base_update(delta_time) end
    end
  end
end
```

```lua
local function create_player(config)
  return entity(
    transform(config.x, config.y),
    health({ max_hp = 100 }),
    click_to_move({ speed = 80 }),
    combat_stats({ atk = 5, def = 2 })
  )
end
```

Key points:
- `entity(...)` in `shared/entity.lua` applies component functions in order. The
  module also exposes helpers: `chain_update`, `chain_init`, `chain_destroy`,
  `chain_update_after`, `declare_component`, `apply_component`.
- Later components access/wrap fields set by earlier ones
- Method chaining via closure wrapping (capture `base_update`, call in new `update`)

### Directory Structure

- `shared/components/` — Component functions (health, transform, combat-stats, aggro, pathfinding, etc.)
- `shared/entities/` — Entity factory functions (player, mob, npc, boss, doppelganger)
- `shared/systems/` — Cross-entity game logic (combat, skill-execution, instincts, etc.)
- `shared/world/` — World container, mob spawner
- `shared/data/` — Static game data (skills, items, mobs, terrains, quests, etc.) with auto-discover loaders
- `shared/net/` — Packet types and message schemas/commands for client↔server protocol
- `shared/constants/` — Enum-like constant modules (skill-types, entity-states, etc.)
- `shared/entity.lua` — Entity composer + chain/declare helpers
- `client/scene.lua` — Scene manager
- `client/scenes/` — Scene definitions; gameplay/ = main game scene
- `client/input/` — Input handling
- `client/ui/` — HUD rendering, transitions, layout system, primitives
- `client/debug/` — Console and debug overlay
- `client/components/` — Rendering components (rect-sprite, camera, name-label, etc.)
- `client/systems/` — Client-side systems (floating-text, particles, effects)
- `client/net/` — Client networking (game-client, prediction, interpolation)
- `client/event-handlers/` — Per-event handlers dispatched off network events
- `client/game/` — Client game logic (shop-cart)

# CLAUDE.md

Guidance for Claude Code (claude.ai/code) working with this repo.

## Project Overview

Botlands = 2D game built with LÖVE 2D (v11.4) and Lua 5.1. Composition-based entity system — entities assembled from reusable component functions.

## Commands

```bash
make run            # Run the game (love .)
make test           # Run all tests (spec then unit)
busted path/to/file_test.lua  # Run a single test file
```

Formatting (`stylua`) and linting (`luacheck`) run auto via PostToolUse hooks on every `.lua` edit — don't run manually. `make check` for CI/manual only.

## Prerequisites

Requires: [LÖVE 2D](https://love2d.org/), luarocks packages `busted`, `luacheck`, `stylua`

## Architecture

### Entity Composition System

Entities = plain tables built by composing component functions. Components = higher-order functions returning mutator function:

```lua
local function health(config)
  return function(entity)
    entity.hp = config.max_hp
    local base_update = entity.update
    function entity.update(delta_time)
      if base_update then base_update(delta_time) end
    end
  end
end
```

```lua
local function create_player(config)
  return entity(
    transform(config.x, config.y),
    health({ max_hp = 100 }),
    click_to_move({ speed = 80 }),
    combat_stats({ atk = 5, def = 2 })
  )
end
```

Key points:
- `entity(...)` in `shared/entity.lua` applies component functions in order. The
  module also exposes helpers: `chain_update`, `chain_init`, `chain_destroy`,
  `chain_update_after`, `declare_component`, `apply_component`.
- Later components access/wrap fields set by earlier ones
- Method chaining via closure wrapping (capture `base_update`, call in new `update`)

### Directory Structure

- `shared/components/` — Component functions (health, transform, combat-stats, aggro, pathfinding, etc.)
- `shared/entities/` — Entity factory functions (player, mob, npc, boss, doppelganger)
- `shared/systems/` — Cross-entity game logic (combat, skill-execution, instincts, etc.)
- `shared/world/` — World container, mob spawner
- `shared/data/` — Static game data (skills, items, mobs, terrains, quests, etc.) with auto-discover loaders
- `shared/net/` — Packet types and message schemas/commands for client↔server protocol
- `shared/constants/` — Enum-like constant modules (skill-types, entity-states, etc.)
- `shared/entity.lua` — Entity composer + chain/declare helpers
- `client/scene.lua` — Scene manager
- `client/scenes/` — Scene definitions; gameplay/ = main game scene
- `client/input/` — Input handling
- `client/ui/` — HUD rendering, transitions, layout system, primitives
- `client/debug/` — Console and debug overlay
- `client/components/` — Rendering components (rect-sprite, camera, name-label, etc.)
- `client/systems/` — Client-side systems (floating-text, particles, effects)
- `client/net/` — Client networking (game-client, prediction, interpolation)
- `client/event-handlers/` — Per-event handlers dispatched off network events
- `client/game/` — Client game logic (shop-cart)
- `server/` — Dedicated-server: command processing, behavior runners, game session, NPC interactions

- `party-set-loot.lua:15`: `loot_type` is only checked to be a non-empty string. `party_manager.set_loot_type` then calls `loot_distribution_types.validate`, which asserts (`party-manager.lua:221`). Any party leader can crash the server this way. Check it in the schema with `loot_distribution_types.is_valid`.
- Same pattern just outside this directory: `server/command-processor.lua:66` runs `assert(slot_data, …)` on a client-supplied `join.slot`.

**3. Respawn works while alive** — `respawn.lua:24-28`
There's no `is_dead` check, and `health.lua:117` resets HP and MP to max and moves the player to the respawn point. Any living player can get a free full heal and teleport, for example to escape combat. Add `if not player.is_dead then return end`.

**4. `interact.skill_level` is never validated** — `interact.lua:67`
It's passed straight to `skill-training.lua:21` as the target level. A client can request any level it chooses, skipping the levels in between and paying only that level's cost. A non-number value could also break the `>=` comparison. Either validate it as a positive integer (and confirm that choosing a level is intended), or drop it from the request.

## Medium

5. **Client data is stored with no limits.** `apply-gearset-rules.lua:173` keeps the client's `rules` table by reference, with no cap on how many sets it holds and extra keys kept. `set-loot-rule` shallow-copies the client's rule, including any unknown fields, into persisted state (`loot-filter.lua:65`). Both let a client make its save data and memory as large as it likes. Copy over only the known fields, and cap the counts.
6. **`use-skill` doesn't validate `target_entity_id`**, which `add-path-waypoint.lua:9-14` does. Whatever value the client sends goes straight to `world:get_entity`.
7. **Some fields are only checked to be a non-empty string.** `unequip.slot_name` should be checked against `equipment_slots.is_valid`, as `apply-gearset-rules` already does, and `party_set_loot.loot_type` has the same gap (item 2).

## Low / cleanup

8. **Layering:** 7 modules under `shared/` require `server.game.*` (instance-manager, party-manager, npc-interactions, treasure-pool-manager). The client doesn't load these modules today, so it works, but command code that only runs on the server sits in `shared/`.
9. `party-decline.lua:34-42` reports `PARTY_INVITE_EXPIRED` with `ok = true` without checking the return value of `decline_invite`.
10. `interact.lua:14-29` writes its own table and `input_tick` checks with an `interact_schema.` error prefix, while every other module uses `common.validate_input_tick`. Since every message except `join` repeats the same `input_tick` check, the check could live in `init.lua` instead.
11. `interact.lua:58` captures `target` when the command is built, and `perform` only rechecks range. It doesn't check whether the NPC has died or despawned since then.
12. `click-move.lua:44` sets the player's private `_walk_speed` field from inside a message handler.

**Missing tests:** none of the command handlers have tests. Item 1 would have been caught by a single test of `instance-entry-respond` with two members.

I'd fix 1–4 first. The existing tests pass (31 of 31), but they only cover validation, so they miss the problems below.

The main finding: neither `server:drain_input_queue()` nor `server:apply_domain_commands()` wraps its calls in `pcall`. So any `assert` or `error` a client can reach crashes the whole server for everyone, not just that client.

## Bugs

**1. Party instance entry never completes, and a denial is never broadcast** (`instance-entry-respond.lua:53-85`)
`instance_manager.respond_party_entry` deletes the pending entry (`pending_party_entries[pending_id] = nil`) before it returns `"denied"` or `"approved"` (`server/game/instance-manager.lua:289, 304`). The handler then calls `get_pending_entry(pending_id)`, which always returns nil in both branches. The result:
- When the last member accepts, nobody enters the instance.
- When someone declines, no one gets `INSTANCE_ENTRY_DENIED`.

Fix: read the entry before calling `respond_party_entry`, or have it return the entry.

**2. Any client can crash the server with a bad `party_set_loot`** (`party-set-loot.lua:15`)
Validation only checks for a non-empty string. `party_manager.set_loot_type` then calls `loot_distribution_types.validate(loot_type)`, which asserts. If a party leader sends `loot_type = "x"`, the server crashes. Fix: validate with `loot_distribution_types.is_valid` in the schema.

**3. Any client can crash the server with an unknown `execute_action`** (`execute-action/init.lua:56`)
An unknown `action` string hits `assert`, not `return false, ...`. `schema_test.lua:102` even tests that it "fails loudly". That makes sense for a programming error, but this value comes straight from the network. Fix: return `false, "execute_action.action: unknown action"`.

**4. Any client can crash the server with `switch_character`** (`switch-character.lua:38`)
`assert(found, ...)` fires on any entity id the client doesn't own. `set-behavior.lua:48` handles the same case properly with `return nil, "entity not owned by client"`; this file should do the same.

**5. A living player can respawn** (`respawn.lua:24-28`)
Nothing checks `player.is_dead`. A client can send `respawn` at any time to get full HP and MP, clear combat, and teleport to the respawn point. Add `if not player.is_dead then return end`, matching `input.lua` and `click-move.lua`.

**6. Kicking from a two-person party leaves the leader uninformed** (`party-kick.lua:65-73`)
When only the leader is left, `party_manager.kick` disbands the party (`party-manager.lua:200-205`). The later `get_party(leader)` call then returns nil, so the leader gets no `PARTY_MEMBER_LEFT` and the client never learns the party is gone. Fix: take a snapshot of the members before kicking, as `party-leave.lua:27` does.

**7. `join` with an empty slot crashes the server** (related; the code is in `command-processor.lua:66`)
`join.lua` only checks for a positive integer. `assert(slot_data, ...)` in the processor then fires for any slot that has no character.

## Smaller issues

- **`party-decline.lua:34-42`** ignores the return value of `decline_invite`. It sends `PARTY_INVITE_EXPIRED` even when the invite didn't exist or belonged to someone else, and the inviter is never told about the decline.
- **`interact.lua:66`** forwards `message.skill_level` to `npc_interactions` without validating it. Also, `perform_err.code` at line 122 will throw if `perform` ever returns `nil, nil`.
- **Unbounded client data gets persisted:**
  - `set-loot-rule.lua` has no limit on how many rules a player can have; any index past the end appends a rule.
  - `apply-gearset-rules.lua` stores the client's `rules` table as-is, including keys the validator never looked at, with no limit on sets or entries.
  - Both are worth limiting and whitelisting, since `mark_dirty` writes them to disk.
- **Inconsistent "invalid input" handling:** some handlers `assert`, some return `nil, err`, some silently do nothing (`set-target.lua:32`, `equip`/`unequip`). Settling on one convention would have prevented bugs 2–4 and 7.
- **Duplicate checks:** `set-behavior.lua:36` and `set-move-mode.lua:26` repeat checks the schema already makes. `cycle-target.lua:13` checks `is_integer` right before an exact `-1`/`1` comparison that already covers it.
- **`interact.lua:14-20`** repeats its own table and `input_tick` checks instead of using `common.validate_input_tick` like every other module, and its error prefixes say `interact_schema.` where the others use `<packet>.`.

I checked `input.lua` for a speed hack via large `move_x`/`move_y` values. It's safe because `movement_math.apply_keyboard` normalizes the direction.

## Recommendation

Fix 1–5 first: 1 breaks a feature outright, 2–4 let any client crash the server, and 5 is an exploit. A `pcall` around `process_message` and `command.execute` in `dedicated-server.lua` would stop the next stray assert from crashing everyone, but it doesn't replace fixing the validators. **4. Any client can crash the server with `switch_character`** (`switch-character.lua:38`)
`assert(found, ...)` fires on any entity id the client doesn't own. `set-behavior.lua:48` handles the same case properly with `return nil, "entity not owned by client"`; this file should do the same.

**5. A living player can respawn** (`respawn.lua:24-28`)
Nothing checks `player.is_dead`. A client can send `respawn` at any time to get full HP and MP, clear combat, and teleport to the respawn point. Add `if not player.is_dead then return end`, matching `input.lua` and `click-move.lua`.

**6. Kicking from a two-person party leaves the leader uninformed** (`party-kick.lua:65-73`)
When only the leader is left, `party_manager.kick` disbands the party (`party-manager.lua:200-205`). The later `get_party(leader)` call then returns nil, so the leader gets no `PARTY_MEMBER_LEFT` and the client never learns the party is gone. Fix: take a snapshot of the members before kicking, as `party-leave.lua:27` does.

**7. `join` with an empty slot crashes the server** (related; the code is in `command-processor.lua:66`)
`join.lua` only checks for a positive integer. `assert(slot_data, ...)` in the processor then fires for any slot that has no character.

## Smaller issues

- **`party-decline.lua:34-42`** ignores the return value of `decline_invite`. It sends `PARTY_INVITE_EXPIRED` even when the invite didn't exist or belonged to someone else, and the inviter is never told about the decline.
- **`interact.lua:66`** forwards `message.skill_level` to `npc_interactions` without validating it. Also, `perform_err.code` at line 122 will throw if `perform` ever returns `nil, nil`.
- **Unbounded client data gets persisted:**
  - `set-loot-rule.lua` has no limit on how many rules a player can have; any index past the end appends a rule.
  - `apply-gearset-rules.lua` stores the client's `rules` table as-is, including keys the validator never looked at, with no limit on sets or entries.
  - Both are worth limiting and whitelisting, since `mark_dirty` writes them to disk.
- **Inconsistent "invalid input" handling:** some handlers `assert`, some return `nil, err`, some silently do nothing (`set-target.lua:32`, `equip`/`unequip`). Settling on one convention would have prevented bugs 2–4 and 7.
- **Duplicate checks:** `set-behavior.lua:36` and `set-move-mode.lua:26` repeat checks the schema already makes. `cycle-target.lua:13` checks `is_integer` right before an exact `-1`/`1` comparison that already covers it.
- **`interact.lua:14-20`** repeats its own table and `input_tick` checks instead of using `common.validate_input_tick` like every other module, and its error prefixes say `interact_schema.` where the others use `<packet>.`.

I checked `input.lua` for a speed hack via large `move_x`/`move_y` values. It's safe because `movement_math.apply_keyboard` normalizes the direction.

## Recommendation

Fix 1–5 first: 1 breaks a feature outright, 2–4 let any client crash the server, and 5 is an exploit. A `pcall` around `process_message` and `command.execute` in `dedicated-server.lua` would stop the next stray assert from crashing everyone, but it doesn't replace fixing the validators. I haven't changed anything. The existing tests pass (31 of 31), but they only cover validation, so they miss the problems below.

The main finding: neither `server:drain_input_queue()` nor `server:apply_domain_commands()` wraps its calls in `pcall`. So any `assert` or `error` a client can reach crashes the whole server for everyone, not just that client.

## Bugs

**1. Party instance entry never completes, and a denial is never broadcast** (`instance-entry-respond.lua:53-85`)
`instance_manager.respond_party_entry` deletes the pending entry (`pending_party_entries[pending_id] = nil`) before it returns `"denied"` or `"approved"` (`server/game/instance-manager.lua:289, 304`). The handler then calls `get_pending_entry(pending_id)`, which always returns nil in both branches. The result:
- When the last member accepts, nobody enters the instance.
- When someone declines, no one gets `INSTANCE_ENTRY_DENIED`.

Fix: read the entry before calling `respond_party_entry`, or have it return the entry.

**2. Any client can crash the server with a bad `party_set_loot`** (`party-set-loot.lua:15`)
Validation only checks for a non-empty string. `party_manager.set_loot_type` then calls `loot_distribution_types.validate(loot_type)`, which asserts. If a party leader sends `loot_type = "x"`, the server crashes. Fix: validate with `loot_distribution_types.is_valid` in the schema.

**3. Any client can crash the server with an unknown `execute_action`** (`execute-action/init.lua:56`)
An unknown `action` string hits `assert`, not `return false, ...`. `schema_test.lua:102` even tests that it "fails loudly". That makes sense for a programming error, but this value comes straight from the network. Fix: return `false, "execute_action.action: unknown action"`.

**4. Any client can crash the server with `switch_character`** (`switch-character.lua:38`)
`assert(found, ...)` fires on any entity id the client doesn't own. `set-behavior.lua:48` handles the same case properly with `return nil, "entity not owned by client"`; this file should do the same.

**5. A living player can respawn** (`respawn.lua:24-28`)
Nothing checks `player.is_dead`. A client can send `respawn` at any time to get full HP and MP, clear combat, and teleport to the respawn point. Add `if not player.is_dead then return end`, matching `input.lua` and `click-move.lua`.

**6. Kicking from a two-person party leaves the leader uninformed** (`party-kick.lua:65-73`)
When only the leader is left, `party_manager.kick` disbands the party (`party-manager.lua:200-205`). The later `get_party(leader)` call then returns nil, so the leader gets no `PARTY_MEMBER_LEFT` and the client never learns the party is gone. Fix: take a snapshot of the members before kicking, as `party-leave.lua:27` does.

**7. `join` with an empty slot crashes the server** (related; the code is in `command-processor.lua:66`)
`join.lua` only checks for a positive integer. `assert(slot_data, ...)` in the processor then fires for any slot that has no character.

## Smaller issues

- **`party-decline.lua:34-42`** ignores the return value of `decline_invite`. It sends `PARTY_INVITE_EXPIRED` even when the invite didn't exist or belonged to someone else, and the inviter is never told about the decline.
- **`interact.lua:66`** forwards `message.skill_level` to `npc_interactions` without validating it. Also, `perform_err.code` at line 122 will throw if `perform` ever returns `nil, nil`.
- **Unbounded client data gets persisted:**
  - `set-loot-rule.lua` has no limit on how many rules a player can have; any index past the end appends a rule.
  - `apply-gearset-rules.lua` stores the client's `rules` table as-is, including keys the validator never looked at, with no limit on sets or entries.
  - Both are worth limiting and whitelisting, since `mark_dirty` writes them to disk.
- **Inconsistent "invalid input" handling:** some handlers `assert`, some return `nil, err`, some silently do nothing (`set-target.lua:32`, `equip`/`unequip`). Settling on one convention would have prevented bugs 2–4 and 7.
- **Duplicate checks:** `set-behavior.lua:36` and `set-move-mode.lua:26` repeat checks the schema already makes. `cycle-target.lua:13` checks `is_integer` right before an exact `-1`/`1` comparison that already covers it.
- **`interact.lua:14-20`** repeats its own table and `input_tick` checks instead of using `common.validate_input_tick` like every other module, and its error prefixes say `interact_schema.` where the others use `<packet>.`.

I checked `input.lua` for a speed hack via large `move_x`/`move_y` values. It's safe because `movement_math.apply_keyboard` normalizes the direction.

## Recommendation

Fix 1–5 first: 1 breaks a feature outright, 2–4 let any client crash the server, and 5 is an exploit. A `pcall` around `process_message` and `command.execute` in `dedicated-server.lua` would stop the next stray assert from crashing everyone, but it doesn't replace fixing the validators. An unknown `action` string hits `assert`, not `return false, ...`. `schema_test.lua:102` even tests that it "fails loudly". That makes sense for a programming error, but this value comes straight from the network. Fix: return `false, "execute_action.action: unknown action"`.

**4. Any client can crash the server with `switch_character`** (`switch-character.lua:38`)
`assert(found, ...)` fires on any entity id the client doesn't own. `set-behavior.lua:48` handles the same case properly with `return nil, "entity not owned by client"`; this file should do the same.

**5. A living player can respawn** (`respawn.lua:24-28`)
Nothing checks `player.is_dead`. A client can send `respawn` at any time to get full HP and MP, clear combat, and teleport to the respawn point. Add `if not player.is_dead then return end`, matching `input.lua` and `click-move.lua`.

**6. Kicking from a two-person party leaves the leader uninformed** (`party-kick.lua:65-73`)
When only the leader is left, `party_manager.kick` disbands the party (`party-manager.lua:200-205`). The later `get_party(leader)` call then returns nil, so the leader gets no `PARTY_MEMBER_LEFT` and the client never learns the party is gone. Fix: take a snapshot of the members before kicking, as `party-leave.lua:27` does.

**7. `join` with an empty slot crashes the server** (related; the code is in `command-processor.lua:66`)
`join.lua` only checks for a positive integer. `assert(slot_data, ...)` in the processor then fires for any slot that has no character.

## Smaller issues

- **`party-decline.lua:34-42`** ignores the return value of `decline_invite`. It sends `PARTY_INVITE_EXPIRED` even when the invite didn't exist or belonged to someone else, and the inviter is never told about the decline.
- **`interact.lua:66`** forwards `message.skill_level` to `npc_interactions` without validating it. Also, `perform_err.code` at line 122 will throw if `perform` ever returns `nil, nil`.
- **Unbounded client data gets persisted:**
  - `set-loot-rule.lua` has no limit on how many rules a player can have; any index past the end appends a rule.
  - `apply-gearset-rules.lua` stores the client's `rules` table as-is, including keys the validator never looked at, with no limit on sets or entries.
  - Both are worth limiting and whitelisting, since `mark_dirty` writes them to disk.
- **Inconsistent "invalid input" handling:** some handlers `assert`, some return `nil, err`, some silently do nothing (`set-target.lua:32`, `equip`/`unequip`). Settling on one convention would have prevented bugs 2–4 and 7.
- **Duplicate checks:** `set-behavior.lua:36` and `set-move-mode.lua:26` repeat checks the schema already makes. `cycle-target.lua:13` checks `is_integer` right before an exact `-1`/`1` comparison that already covers it.
- **`interact.lua:14-20`** repeats its own table and `input_tick` checks instead of using `common.validate_input_tick` like every other module, and its error prefixes say `interact_schema.` where the others use `<packet>.`.

I checked `input.lua` for a speed hack via large `move_x`/`move_y` values. It's safe because `movement_math.apply_keyboard` normalizes the direction.

## Recommendation

Fix 1–5 first: 1 breaks a feature outright, 2–4 let any client crash the server, and 5 is an exploit. A `pcall` around `process_message` and `command.execute` in `dedicated-server.lua` would stop the next stray assert from crashing everyone, but it doesn't replace fixing the validators. I haven't changed anything. {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CgZqKY7KtaQ2LoESe7xta","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"# Review: `shared/net/messages/client-to-server`

I read all 29 top-level modules, `execute-action/init.lua` and its 12 actions, and followed calls into `command-processor`, `command-builder`, `dedicated-server`, `party-manager`, `instance-manager` and the player components. The existing tests pass (10/10 with `busted -p _test`), but none of them cover the issues below.

**Context for the critical items:** nothing on the path from `server:process_message` through `validate`, `build` and `execute` is wrapped in `pcall`. Any `assert` or runtime error that client input can trigger therefore throws out of `server:step()` and stops the tick for everyone.

## Critical: a client can crash the server

1. **Unknown `execute_action` action**: `execute-action/init.lua:56` calls `assert(action_validate, "unhandled execute_action type: ...")`. Sending `{type="EXECUTE_ACTION", input_tick=1, action="x"}` takes the server down. It should be `return false, "execute_action.action: unknown action"`.
2. **`switch_character` with an entity you don't own**: `switch-character.lua:38` calls `assert(found, ...)`. It should return `nil, "entity not owned by client"`, the same way `set-behavior.lua:48` does.
3. **`party_set_loot` with an invalid loot type**: validation only checks for a non-empty string (`party-set-loot.lua:15`). Then `party_manager.set_loot_type` calls `loot_distribution_types.validate()`, which is a `define()` validator that **asserts** (`shared/constants/define.lua:8`). Any party leader can crash the server. Fix it in the schema with `loot_distribution_types.is_valid(message.loot_type)`.
4. The assertions on `owned_entities` in `build` (`flee.lua:21`, `set-behavior.lua:34`, `set-move-mode.lua:29`, `switch-character.lua:29`) can't be reached today because `require_player` runs first. That's fine, but it only holds while `join` stays the only path that sets `player`.

Adjacent but outside this directory: `command-processor.lua:66` calls `assert(slot_data, "JOIN: no character at slot ...")`, so `join` with `slot = 999` crashes the server too.

## High: logic bugs

5. **Party instance entry is broken in both branches** (`instance-entry-respond.lua:53-85`). `instance_manager.respond_party_entry` sets `pending_party_entries[pending_id] = nil` before it returns `"denied"` or `"approved"` (`instance-manager.lua:289, 304`). The handler then calls `get_pending_entry(pending_id)`, gets `nil`, and does nothing. As a result:
   - On a denial, no one is notified.
   - On approval, **no one enters the instance**.
   
   Fix: have `respond_party_entry` return the entry along with the status, or read the entry before responding.
6. **`respawn` doesn't check that the player is dead** (`respawn.lua:24-29`). `e:respawn` restores HP and MP to full and teleports the player to the nearest respawn point. Any live player can send it at any time for a free full heal and an escape from combat. Add `if not player.is_dead then return end`.

## Medium

7. **`party_decline` always reports success** (`party-decline.lua:34-42`). It ignores the return value of `decline_invite`, so declining someone else's invite id or a made-up one still sends `PARTY_INVITE_EXPIRED`. The inviter is also never told the invite was declined.
8. **`party_kick` gives the kicker no feedback when the party disbands** (`party-kick.lua:65-73`). Kicking from a two-person party clears the party in `party_manager.kick`, so `get_party` returns nil and the leader gets no event.
9. **`interact` checks the target at build time and holds onto it.** `interact.lua:58` captures the entity, which can die or despawn before `execute`. `npc_interactions.perform` does re-check `can_interact`, so this is probably safe in practice. However, `skill_level` (line 67) is passed into the request without being validated.
10. **`interact` is the only schema that skips `common.validate_input_tick`** (`interact.lua:15-21`). It also only checks that `request_id` is non-empty, with no length limit, and that string is echoed back to the client.
11. **`apply_gearset_rules` has no size limits.** The client sends `sets`, `per_skill`, set names and the nesting depth, all unbounded, and the table is stored by reference on the player (`gearswap.lua:92`). Add caps on the number of sets and the length of names.

- `use-skill.lua`: `message.target_entity_id` is never validated by the action schema. `add-path-waypoint` validates the same field. Also, `level_data.range > 0` at line 56 errors if a level definition has no `range`.

I read all 29 top-level modules, `execute-action/init.lua` and its 12 actions, and followed calls into `command-processor`, `command-builder`, `dedicated-server`, `party-manager`, `instance-manager` and the player components. The existing tests pass (10/10 with `busted -p _test`), but none of them cover the issues below.

**Context for the critical items:** nothing on the path from `server:process_message` through `validate`, `build` and `execute` is wrapped in `pcall`. Any `assert` or runtime error that client input can trigger therefore throws out of `server:step()` and stops the tick for everyone.

## Critical: a client can crash the server

1. **Unknown `execute_action` action**: `execute-action/init.lua:56` calls `assert(action_validate, "unhandled execute_action type: ...")`. Sending `{type="EXECUTE_ACTION", input_tick=1, action="x"}` takes the server down. It should be `return false, "execute_action.action: unknown action"`.
2. **`switch_character` with an entity you don't own**: `switch-character.lua:38` calls `assert(found, ...)`. It should return `nil, "entity not owned by client"`, the same way `set-behavior.lua:48` does.
3. **`party_set_loot` with an invalid loot type**: validation only checks for a non-empty string (`party-set-loot.lua:15`). Then `party_manager.set_loot_type` calls `loot_distribution_types.validate()`, which is a `define()` validator that **asserts** (`shared/constants/define.lua:8`). Any party leader can crash the server. Fix it in the schema with `loot_distribution_types.is_valid(message.loot_type)`.
4. The assertions on `owned_entities` in `build` (`flee.lua:21`, `set-behavior.lua:34`, `set-move-mode.lua:29`, `switch-character.lua:29`) can't be reached today because `require_player` runs first. That's fine, but it only holds while `join` stays the only path that sets `player`.

Adjacent but outside this directory: `command-processor.lua:66` calls `assert(slot_data, "JOIN: no character at slot ...")`, so `join` with `slot = 999` crashes the server too.

## High: logic bugs

5. **Party instance entry is broken in both branches** (`instance-entry-respond.lua:53-85`). `instance_manager.respond_party_entry` sets `pending_party_entries[pending_id] = nil` before it returns `"denied"` or `"approved"` (`instance-manager.lua:289, 304`). The handler then calls `get_pending_entry(pending_id)`, gets `nil`, and does nothing. As a result:
   - On a denial, no one is notified.
   - On approval, **no one enters the instance**.
   
   Fix: have `respond_party_entry` return the entry along with the status, or read the entry before responding.
6. **`respawn` doesn't check that the player is dead** (`respawn.lua:24-29`). `e:respawn` restores HP and MP to full and teleports the player to the nearest respawn point. Any live player can send it at any time for a free full heal and an escape from combat. Add `if not player.is_dead then return end`.

## Medium

7. **`party_decline` always reports success** (`party-decline.lua:34-42`). It ignores the return value of `decline_invite`, so declining someone else's invite id or a made-up one still sends `PARTY_INVITE_EXPIRED`. The inviter is also never told the invite was declined.

10. **`interact` is the only schema that skips `common.validate_input_tick`** (`interact.lua:15-21`). It also only checks that `request_id` is non-empty, with no length limit, and that string is echoed back to the client.

4. The assertions on `owned_entities` in `build` (`flee.lua:21`, `set-behavior.lua:34`, `set-move-mode.lua:29`, `switch-character.lua:29`) can't be reached today because `require_player` runs first. That's fine, but it only holds while `join` stays the only path that sets `player`.

The handler then calls `get_pending_entry(pending_id)`, gets `nil`, and does nothing. As a result:
   - On a denial, no one is notified.
   - On approval, **no one enters the instance**.
   
   Fix: have `respond_party_entry` return the entry along with the status, or read the entry before responding.
6. **`respawn` doesn't check that the player is dead** (`respawn.lua:24-29`). `e:respawn` restores HP and MP to full and teleports the player to the nearest respawn point. Any live player can send it at any time for a free full heal and an escape from combat. Add `if not player.is_dead then return end`.

## Medium

7. **`party_decline` always reports success** (`party-decline.lua:34-42`). It ignores the return value of `decline_invite`, so declining someone else's invite id or a made-up one still sends `PARTY_INVITE_EXPIRED`. The inviter is also never told the invite was declined.
8. **`party_kick` gives the kicker no feedback when the party disbands** (`party-kick.lua:65-73`). Kicking from a two-person party clears the party in `party_manager.kick`, so `get_party` returns nil and the leader gets no event.
9. **`interact` checks the target at build time and holds onto it.** `interact.lua:58` captures the entity, which can die or despawn before `execute`. `npc_interactions.perform` does re-check `can_interact`, so this is probably safe in practice. 10. **`interact` is the only schema that skips `common.validate_input_tick`** (`interact.lua:15-21`). It also only checks that `request_id` is non-empty, with no length limit, and that string is echoed back to the client.

# Review

Reads a change the way a second engineer would and returns **findings**: each one located, verified in the code, and paired with the concrete move that fixes it. The review changes nothing; the caller decides what to apply. It looks for bugs (does the code do what its callers assume, on every input they can send?), shape (is the code modular and composed?) and cost (what does it do at scale?). To keep the reading out of a busy context, dispatch a `kit:reviewer` agent with the target instead of reviewing inline; `coordinate` always does.

## Steps

1. **Scope.** Take the target from `shared/systems/skill-execution/_internal.lua`: a diff, a PR number, a branch, or a path. With none, review the working tree against the base branch (`git diff <base>...HEAD` plus uncommitted changes). Read `git diff --stat`, then every hunk. Then read past the diff: each changed public surface's callers and callees, far enough to see every boundary the change crosses. If the plan holds a `## Code Shape`, read the part this change implements; it is the contract the change is held to. When the target is a module rather than a change, list what it owns before reading for problems: each group of functions and the state it keeps. Done when every changed file and every boundary it crosses has been read.
2. **Look through each lens.** Walk the change once per lens (Correct, Modular, Composed, Cheap) and write down every candidate, with the line that triggered it. The Correct pass is a hunt, not a glance: for each procedure, pick the inputs its callers can send and the ones today's data never does, and follow them through.
3. **Verify.** For each candidate, confirm the problem in the code rather than the diff: trace a concrete call path or input that hits it. For a cost candidate, name the scale at which it matters (per frame, per request, per row, n of what). A candidate that doesn't survive is dropped; the review's value is that every finding is real.
4. **Rank.** Order by consequence: a bug that today's inputs can hit, a bug that waits on a planned change, then a boundary the change damages (a contract broken, a dependency reversed, a leak of internals), then coupling that will spread, then cost at a scale the project reaches, then local shape. Keep the findings worth acting on; a nit that changes nothing for the next reader is cut.
5. **Report** in the Findings format, and end the turn without editing. Under `coordinate`, the report is the whole final message. Standalone, end the turn asking which findings to apply, as a review ([asking](../../references/asking.md)): "Reply with the numbers to apply."

## Correct

Does the code do what its callers assume, for every input they can send, including the ones today's data never sends. Each candidate is traced on a concrete input before it becomes a finding.

- **Holds only today.** Code that is right because a constant is 1, a list has one element, a level is the only level, or an enum has its current members. Name the constant or data that makes it pass, and what breaks when it changes: a loop that ignores its index, a lookup that returns the first match, a height that assumes one floor. Propose the real handling or an assertion that fails loudly when the assumption breaks.
- **Two definitions of one rule.** A fact computed in two places (a count, a threshold, a "can this happen" check) with different conditions in each, so the two can disagree. Trace one input through both.
- **Edges.** Empty, one, the boundary value, the last index, negative, zero, the maximum: for each loop and slice, say what happens at the ends.
- **Order of operations.** A fallible step before a branch that doesn't need it; a check after the write it should guard; a state read before the update that changes it.
- **State.** For each state machine or lifecycle, the transition that isn't handled, the state nothing resets, the resource nothing releases.
- **Numbers.** Float equality, depth or z values that coincide, integer division, unit mismatches, overflow at the project's actual sizes.
- **Weak or missing tests.** A test that passes for the wrong reason (it asks for n and checks element 0; it mocks the thing under test), or logic with branching the tests never reach.

## Modular

One owner per concept, dependencies one way, contracts at the boundaries. The rules of a boundary live in `architect`'s Boundaries section (`../architect/SKILL.md`); this lens checks the change against them.

- **Several owners in one file.** A module whose functions fall into distinct groups (validate, charge, compute, orchestrate), each a section with its own helpers and state, is several modules in one file: every change to one group is a change to the file every group's caller depends on. Name the groups and propose the split, keeping the public names through a facade.
- **Reaching in.** A change that reads another module's private state, its file layout, its ordering or its error text, is coupling to something the owner may change. The move: ask the owner for an operation that gives the fact needed.
- **A new arrow.** Every new import or call across modules is a dependency arrow. One that points against the existing direction, or closes a cycle, is a finding whatever the convenience.
- **Contract drift.** A boundary that now exposes more than the consumer needs (a whole record where an id would do, a mutable collection where a copy or an iterator would do) widens what consumers can depend on.
- **Generic with one consumer.** A new generic shape (`Pool<T>`, a plugin registry, an options object with one caller) with a single consumer and no named future one is speculation that every reader must now understand.
- **Duplicate with two consumers.** The same logic appearing in a second place is an extraction that is due; the third is overdue. Two similar lines are not a duplicate.
- **No seam.** A change testable only by reaching into internals (private fields, module state, a mocked import) is missing a seam: the dependency it should take as a parameter.

## Composed

Small agnostic parts, assembled at the call site into the thing needed, over one big part configured by flags. The test is **case or part**: a *case* is another value that selects behaviour, and belongs in a variant, a strategy or a lookup table; a *part* is another region of work, and belongs in a sibling the caller composes.

- **Flags.** A boolean parameter that switches which code runs is two functions welded together; the caller should call the one it means. Three boolean parameters is a type that hasn't been named.
- **Growing options.** An options object gaining fields with each feature is a part being smuggled in as configuration.
- **Inheritance for reuse.** A subclass that exists to share code, not to be substituted, is composition done with the wrong tool: hold the shared piece, don't extend it.
- **Reaching out.** A function that fetches its own dependencies (a global, a singleton, a service locator, the clock, the filesystem) can't be composed with a different one. Take them as parameters.
- **Pure core, effects at the edge.** Logic that interleaves computation with I/O, time or randomness can be neither tested in isolation nor reused. Separate the decision from the act.
- **Long functions.** A function that does a sequence of distinct things reads as a script; each thing is a part with a name. The smell is the comment that introduces each section.

## Cheap

Static reasoning about what the code does at scale. Every finding names the scale that makes it matter; `perf` owns measurement, and a finding whose fix is a trade-off recommends measuring rather than asserting.

- **Work in the hot path.** Allocation, string building, regex compilation, logging, synchronous I/O inside a per-frame, per-request or per-row loop.
- **Shape mismatch.** A lookup in a list where a map is due, nested loops over the same collection, a sort or a full scan inside a loop, a recomputation of a value the loop doesn't change.
- **Chatty boundary.** One call per item across a process, network or database boundary (N+1). Batch, join or prefetch.
- **Unbounded growth.** A cache with no eviction, a listener never removed, a collection that only ever grows, a retry with no cap.
- **Needless copies.** Cloning a structure to read it, serialising to compare, converting between representations at every step instead of once at the edge.
- **Serial waits.** Independent async work awaited one after the other; blocking work on the main or event thread.

## Findings

Ranked and numbered, so the caller can answer with numbers. Each finding carries a location, the evidence, the consequence, and the move:

- A finding without a concrete change is an observation; cut it or find the move.
- Bugs go first, marked **Bug** in the title; a bug that today's data can't reach is marked **Latent** and says what unlocks it.
- Clean is a valid result: "No findings" with one line on what was checked.

## Done when

Every changed file and crossed boundary has been read, every finding is verified in the code with a location and a change, the list is ranked, and nothing was edited.

3. **Latent: weapon skills never set a cooldown or reset `cast_initial_mp_deducted`** — `_internal.lua:259-337`

4. **Latent: weapon skills spend TP before checking for arrows** — `_internal.lua:260-267`
   `consume_tp()` runs first. If the bow check then fails, the function returns nil, so the player loses all their TP and gets no event and no log line. No weapon skill allows `BOW` in `required_weapon_types` today, so this can't happen yet. The first bow weapon skill will hit it when arrows run out.
   **Fix:** run the arrow check before `consume_tp()`. Better still, move it into `validate_completion` next to the TP check.

5. **Latent: the bow check is half dead code** — `_internal.lua:264`
   `is_bow and not is_magical_formula(skill)`: this function only runs for `WEAPON_SKILL`, so `is_magical_formula` is always false. It reads as if a magical weapon skill could skip arrows, but there is no such path.

# Review

Reads a change the way a second engineer would and returns **findings**: each one located, verified in the code, and paired with the concrete move that fixes it. The review changes nothing; the caller decides what to apply. It looks for bugs (does the code do what its callers assume, on every input they can send?), shape (is the code modular and composed?) and cost (what does it do at scale?). To keep the reading out of a busy context, dispatch a `kit:reviewer` agent with the target instead of reviewing inline; `coordinate` always does.

## Steps

1. **Scope.** Take the target from `shared/systems/skill-execution/_internal.lua`: a diff, a PR number, a branch, or a path. With none, review the working tree against the base branch (`git diff <base>...HEAD` plus uncommitted changes). Read `git diff --stat`, then every hunk. Then read past the diff: each changed public surface's callers and callees, far enough to see every boundary the change crosses. If the plan holds a `## Code Shape`, read the part this change implements; it is the contract the change is held to. When the target is a module rather than a change, list what it owns before reading for problems: each group of functions and the state it keeps. Done when every changed file and every boundary it crosses has been read.
2. **Look through each lens.** Walk the change once per lens (Correct, Modular, Composed, Cheap) and write down every candidate, with the line that triggered it. The Correct pass is a hunt, not a glance: for each procedure, pick the inputs its callers can send and the ones today's data never does, and follow them through.
3. **Verify.** For each candidate, confirm the problem in the code rather than the diff: trace a concrete call path or input that hits it. For a cost candidate, name the scale at which it matters (per frame, per request, per row, n of what). A candidate that doesn't survive is dropped; the review's value is that every finding is real.
4. **Rank.** Order by consequence: a bug that today's inputs can hit, a bug that waits on a planned change, then a boundary the change damages (a contract broken, a dependency reversed, a leak of internals), then coupling that will spread, then cost at a scale the project reaches, then local shape. Keep the findings worth acting on; a nit that changes nothing for the next reader is cut.
5. **Report** in the Findings format, and end the turn without editing. Under `coordinate`, the report is the whole final message. Standalone, end the turn asking which findings to apply, as a review ([asking](../../references/asking.md)): "Reply with the numbers to apply."

## Correct

Does the code do what its callers assume, for every input they can send, including the ones today's data never sends. Each candidate is traced on a concrete input before it becomes a finding.

- **Holds only today.** Code that is right because a constant is 1, a list has one element, a level is the only level, or an enum has its current members. Name the constant or data that makes it pass, and what breaks when it changes: a loop that ignores its index, a lookup that returns the first match, a height that assumes one floor. Propose the real handling or an assertion that fails loudly when the assumption breaks.
- **Two definitions of one rule.** A fact computed in two places (a count, a threshold, a "can this happen" check) with different conditions in each, so the two can disagree. Trace one input through both.
- **Edges.** Empty, one, the boundary value, the last index, negative, zero, the maximum: for each loop and slice, say what happens at the ends.
- **Order of operations.** A fallible step before a branch that doesn't need it; a check after the write it should guard; a state read before the update that changes it.
- **State.** For each state machine or lifecycle, the transition that isn't handled, the state nothing resets, the resource nothing releases.
- **Numbers.** Float equality, depth or z values that coincide, integer division, unit mismatches, overflow at the project's actual sizes.
- **Weak or missing tests.** A test that passes for the wrong reason (it asks for n and checks element 0; it mocks the thing under test), or logic with branching the tests never reach.

## Modular

One owner per concept, dependencies one way, contracts at the boundaries. The rules of a boundary live in `architect`'s Boundaries section (`../architect/SKILL.md`); this lens checks the change against them.

- **Several owners in one file.** A module whose functions fall into distinct groups (validate, charge, compute, orchestrate), each a section with its own helpers and state, is several modules in one file: every change to one group is a change to the file every group's caller depends on. Name the groups and propose the split, keeping the public names through a facade.
- **Reaching in.** A change that reads another module's private state, its file layout, its ordering or its error text, is coupling to something the owner may change. The move: ask the owner for an operation that gives the fact needed.
- **A new arrow.** Every new import or call across modules is a dependency arrow. One that points against the existing direction, or closes a cycle, is a finding whatever the convenience.
- **Contract drift.** A boundary that now exposes more than the consumer needs (a whole record where an id would do, a mutable collection where a copy or an iterator would do) widens what consumers can depend on.
- **Generic with one consumer.** A new generic shape (`Pool<T>`, a plugin registry, an options object with one caller) with a single consumer and no named future one is speculation that every reader must now understand.
- **Duplicate with two consumers.** The same logic appearing in a second place is an extraction that is due; the third is overdue. Two similar lines are not a duplicate.
- **No seam.** A change testable only by reaching into internals (private fields, module state, a mocked import) is missing a seam: the dependency it should take as a parameter.

## Composed

Small agnostic parts, assembled at the call site into the thing needed, over one big part configured by flags. The test is **case or part**: a *case* is another value that selects behaviour, and belongs in a variant, a strategy or a lookup table; a *part* is another region of work, and belongs in a sibling the caller composes.

- **Flags.** A boolean parameter that switches which code runs is two functions welded together; the caller should call the one it means. Three boolean parameters is a type that hasn't been named.
- **Growing options.** An options object gaining fields with each feature is a part being smuggled in as configuration.
- **Inheritance for reuse.** A subclass that exists to share code, not to be substituted, is composition done with the wrong tool: hold the shared piece, don't extend it.
- **Reaching out.** A function that fetches its own dependencies (a global, a singleton, a service locator, the clock, the filesystem) can't be composed with a different one. Take them as parameters.
- **Pure core, effects at the edge.** Logic that interleaves computation with I/O, time or randomness can be neither tested in isolation nor reused. Separate the decision from the act.
- **Long functions.** A function that does a sequence of distinct things reads as a script; each thing is a part with a name. The smell is the comment that introduces each section.

## Cheap

Static reasoning about what the code does at scale. Every finding names the scale that makes it matter; `perf` owns measurement, and a finding whose fix is a trade-off recommends measuring rather than asserting.

- **Work in the hot path.** Allocation, string building, regex compilation, logging, synchronous I/O inside a per-frame, per-request or per-row loop.
- **Shape mismatch.** A lookup in a list where a map is due, nested loops over the same collection, a sort or a full scan inside a loop, a recomputation of a value the loop doesn't change.
- **Chatty boundary.** One call per item across a process, network or database boundary (N+1). Batch, join or prefetch.
- **Unbounded growth.** A cache with no eviction, a listener never removed, a collection that only ever grows, a retry with no cap.
- **Needless copies.** Cloning a structure to read it, serialising to compare, converting between representations at every step instead of once at the edge.
- **Serial waits.** Independent async work awaited one after the other; blocking work on the main or event thread.

## Findings

Ranked and numbered, so the caller can answer with numbers. Each finding carries a location, the evidence, the consequence, and the move:

```markdown
## Findings

1. **Crew reads the job board's internal list** — `src/crew.js:42`
   `crew.tick` iterates `board._jobs` to find idle work, so the board can't change its storage without breaking crew. Change: add `board.next_open(kind)` and call it here.
2. **One render allocates a closure per cell** — `src/grid.js:118`
   `cells.map(c => () => draw(c))` runs per frame over 4,000 cells. Change: draw in the loop directly, or build the closures once when the grid changes.

Seen, no action: the `Hotel` import in `economy.js` is unused since this change.
```

- A finding without a concrete change is an observation; cut it or find the move.
- Bugs go first, marked **Bug** in the title; a bug that today's data can't reach is marked **Latent** and says what unlocks it.
- Clean is a valid result: "No findings" with one line on what was checked.

## Done when

Every changed file and crossed boundary has been read, every finding is verified in the code with a location and a change, the list is ranked, and nothing was edited.

   `calculate_skill_damage` uses up the active shot every time it's called. `apply_weapon_skill_damage` calls it once per hit and only reloads after the loop (`:333`). Concrete case: Shadow Barrage (`hit_count = 7`) with a soulshot loaded. Hit 1 gets `item.damage_multiplier`. On hits 2–7, `consume_active_shot` returns nil, so the multiplier is 1.0.    **Fix:** use up the shot once, before the loop, and pass the multiplier into a calculation that has no side effects. See #6.

2. **Bug: the hit count in the log and the event is wrong when the target dies partway through** — `_internal.lua:279-296`, `:324`
   The loop stops when the target dies (`:283`). But `hits_msg`, the log's `hit_count` and `event.hit_count` all use `hits`, the planned count. If Shadow Barrage kills on hit 3, the log says "(7x)".
   **Fix:** count the hits that actually landed inside the loop and report that number.

3. **Latent: weapon skills never set a cooldown or reset `cast_initial_mp_deducted`** — `_internal.lua:259-337`
   The spell path calls `deduct_mp_and_set_cooldown` (`:227`). The weapon path doesn't, and it doesn't go through `_run` either. Today every weapon skill has `cooldown = 0` and `mp_cost = 0`, so nothing visible breaks. The first weapon skill with a nonzero cooldown will have none, because `skill-castability.lua:63` reads a value that is never written. Its `cooldown_group` would also be ignored.
   **Fix:** call `deduct_mp_and_set_cooldown` in `apply_weapon_skill_damage` (and drop any MP part if weapon skills shouldn't cost MP).

   `consume_tp()` runs first. If the bow check then fails, the function returns nil, so the player loses all their TP and gets no event and no log line. No weapon skill allows `BOW` in `required_weapon_types` today, so this can't happen yet. The first bow weapon skill will hit it when arrows run out.
   **Fix:** run the arrow check before `consume_tp()`. Better still, move it into `validate_completion` next to the TP check.

5. **Latent: the bow check is half dead code** — `_internal.lua:264`
   `is_bow and not is_magical_formula(skill)`: this function only runs for `WEAPON_SKILL`, so `is_magical_formula` is always false. It reads as if a magical weapon skill could skip arrows, but there is no such path.
   **Fix:** use `local is_bow_skill = is_bow`, or write down the actual rule if magical weapon skills are planned.

6. **The damage calculation changes the player's inventory, so each caller has to work around it** — `_internal.lua:166-217`
   `calculate_skill_damage` uses up a shot as a side effect. That is what causes #1. It is also why `drain.lua:13` must pass `consume_shot = false` to avoid using two shots. Any future status skill that calls `primitives.calculate_damage` without that flag would also use two. Shot handling now lives in three places: `consume_shot_for_skill`, inside the calculation, and the reloads hard-coded at `:244` and `:333`.
   **Fix:** have `calculate_skill_damage(entity, target, skill, level_data, multiplier)` only compute. Add one `take_shot(entity, skill) -> multiplier, consumed` next to `consume_shot_for_skill`. Each handler (spell, weapon, drain) then takes the shot once and reloads once.

7. **`_internal` mixes small helpers with two complete skill handlers** — `_internal.lua:225-337`
   Most of the file is helpers: validation, cost and cooldown, shots, damage math, logging and events. `apply_spell_damage` and `apply_weapon_skill_damage` are full skill flows. Every other subtype gets its cost → effect → log → event sequence from `_run`; these two rewrite it by hand. Rewriting it is how the weapon path lost the cooldown step (#3).
   **Fix:** move both handlers into a `_damage.lua` that `_primitives.apply_damage` dispatches to. Have each one either go through `_run.run` or at least make the same `deduct_mp_and_set_cooldown` call. That leaves `_internal` with only the helpers.

# Review

Reads a change the way a second engineer would and returns **findings**: each one located, verified in the code, and paired with the concrete move that fixes it. The review changes nothing; the caller decides what to apply. It looks for bugs (does the code do what its callers assume, on every input they can send?), shape (is the code modular and composed?) and cost (what does it do at scale?). To keep the reading out of a busy context, dispatch a `kit:reviewer` agent with the target instead of reviewing inline; `coordinate` always does.

## Steps

1. **Scope.** Take the target from `shared/systems/skill-execution/_internal.lua`: a diff, a PR number, a branch, or a path. With none, review the working tree against the base branch (`git diff <base>...HEAD` plus uncommitted changes). Read `git diff --stat`, then every hunk. Then read past the diff: each changed public surface's callers and callees, far enough to see every boundary the change crosses. If the plan holds a `## Code Shape`, read the part this change implements; it is the contract the change is held to. When the target is a module rather than a change, list what it owns before reading for problems: each group of functions and the state it keeps. Done when every changed file and every boundary it crosses has been read.
2. **Look through each lens.** Walk the change once per lens (Correct, Modular, Composed, Cheap) and write down every candidate, with the line that triggered it. The Correct pass is a hunt, not a glance: for each procedure, pick the inputs its callers can send and the ones today's data never does, and follow them through.
3. **Verify.** For each candidate, confirm the problem in the code rather than the diff: trace a concrete call path or input that hits it. For a cost candidate, name the scale at which it matters (per frame, per request, per row, n of what). A candidate that doesn't survive is dropped; the review's value is that every finding is real.
4. **Rank.** Order by consequence: a bug that today's inputs can hit, a bug that waits on a planned change, then a boundary the change damages (a contract broken, a dependency reversed, a leak of internals), then coupling that will spread, then cost at a scale the project reaches, then local shape. Keep the findings worth acting on; a nit that changes nothing for the next reader is cut.
5. **Report** in the Findings format, and end the turn without editing. Under `coordinate`, the report is the whole final message. Standalone, end the turn asking which findings to apply, as a review ([asking](../../references/asking.md)): "Reply with the numbers to apply."

## Correct

Does the code do what its callers assume, for every input they can send, including the ones today's data never sends. Each candidate is traced on a concrete input before it becomes a finding.

- **Holds only today.** Code that is right because a constant is 1, a list has one element, a level is the only level, or an enum has its current members. Name the constant or data that makes it pass, and what breaks when it changes: a loop that ignores its index, a lookup that returns the first match, a height that assumes one floor. Propose the real handling or an assertion that fails loudly when the assumption breaks.
- **Two definitions of one rule.** A fact computed in two places (a count, a threshold, a "can this happen" check) with different conditions in each, so the two can disagree. Trace one input through both.
- **Edges.** Empty, one, the boundary value, the last index, negative, zero, the maximum: for each loop and slice, say what happens at the ends.
- **Order of operations.** A fallible step before a branch that doesn't need it; a check after the write it should guard; a state read before the update that changes it.
- **State.** For each state machine or lifecycle, the transition that isn't handled, the state nothing resets, the resource nothing releases.
- **Numbers.** Float equality, depth or z values that coincide, integer division, unit mismatches, overflow at the project's actual sizes.
- **Weak or missing tests.** A test that passes for the wrong reason (it asks for n and checks element 0; it mocks the thing under test), or logic with branching the tests never reach.

## Modular

One owner per concept, dependencies one way, contracts at the boundaries. The rules of a boundary live in `architect`'s Boundaries section (`../architect/SKILL.md`); this lens checks the change against them.

- **Several owners in one file.** A module whose functions fall into distinct groups (validate, charge, compute, orchestrate), each a section with its own helpers and state, is several modules in one file: every change to one group is a change to the file every group's caller depends on. Name the groups and propose the split, keeping the public names through a facade.
- **Reaching in.** A change that reads another module's private state, its file layout, its ordering or its error text, is coupling to something the owner may change. The move: ask the owner for an operation that gives the fact needed.
- **A new arrow.** Every new import or call across modules is a dependency arrow. One that points against the existing direction, or closes a cycle, is a finding whatever the convenience.
- **Contract drift.** A boundary that now exposes more than the consumer needs (a whole record where an id would do, a mutable collection where a copy or an iterator would do) widens what consumers can depend on.
- **Generic with one consumer.** A new generic shape (`Pool<T>`, a plugin registry, an options object with one caller) with a single consumer and no named future one is speculation that every reader must now understand.
- **Duplicate with two consumers.** The same logic appearing in a second place is an extraction that is due; the third is overdue. Two similar lines are not a duplicate.
- **No seam.** A change testable only by reaching into internals (private fields, module state, a mocked import) is missing a seam: the dependency it should take as a parameter.

## Composed

Small agnostic parts, assembled at the call site into the thing needed, over one big part configured by flags. The test is **case or part**: a *case* is another value that selects behaviour, and belongs in a variant, a strategy or a lookup table; a *part* is another region of work, and belongs in a sibling the caller composes.

- **Flags.** A boolean parameter that switches which code runs is two functions welded together; the caller should call the one it means. Three boolean parameters is a type that hasn't been named.
- **Growing options.** An options object gaining fields with each feature is a part being smuggled in as configuration.
- **Inheritance for reuse.** A subclass that exists to share code, not to be substituted, is composition done with the wrong tool: hold the shared piece, don't extend it.
- **Reaching out.** A function that fetches its own dependencies (a global, a singleton, a service locator, the clock, the filesystem) can't be composed with a different one. Take them as parameters.
- **Pure core, effects at the edge.** Logic that interleaves computation with I/O, time or randomness can be neither tested in isolation nor reused. Separate the decision from the act.
- **Long functions.** A function that does a sequence of distinct things reads as a script; each thing is a part with a name. The smell is the comment that introduces each section.

## Cheap

Static reasoning about what the code does at scale. Every finding names the scale that makes it matter; `perf` owns measurement, and a finding whose fix is a trade-off recommends measuring rather than asserting.

- **Work in the hot path.** Allocation, string building, regex compilation, logging, synchronous I/O inside a per-frame, per-request or per-row loop.
- **Shape mismatch.** A lookup in a list where a map is due, nested loops over the same collection, a sort or a full scan inside a loop, a recomputation of a value the loop doesn't change.
- **Chatty boundary.** One call per item across a process, network or database boundary (N+1). Batch, join or prefetch.
- **Unbounded growth.** A cache with no eviction, a listener never removed, a collection that only ever grows, a retry with no cap.
- **Needless copies.** Cloning a structure to read it, serialising to compare, converting between representations at every step instead of once at the edge.
- **Serial waits.** Independent async work awaited one after the other; blocking work on the main or event thread.

## Findings

Ranked and numbered, so the caller can answer with numbers. Each finding carries a location, the evidence, the consequence, and the move:

```markdown
## Findings

1. **Crew reads the job board's internal list** — `src/crew.js:42`
   `crew.tick` iterates `board._jobs` to find idle work, so the board can't change its storage without breaking crew. Change: add `board.next_open(kind)` and call it here.
2. **One render allocates a closure per cell** — `src/grid.js:118`
   `cells.map(c => () => draw(c))` runs per frame over 4,000 cells. Change: draw in the loop directly, or build the closures once when the grid changes.

Seen, no action: the `Hotel` import in `economy.js` is unused since this change.
```

- A finding without a concrete change is an observation; cut it or find the move.
- Bugs go first, marked **Bug** in the title; a bug that today's data can't reach is marked **Latent** and says what unlocks it.
- Clean is a valid result: "No findings" with one line on what was checked.

## Done when

Every changed file and crossed boundary has been read, every finding is verified in the code with a location and a change, the list is ranked, and nothing was edited.

local formulas = require("shared.data.stat-formulas")
local logger = require("shared.lib.logger")
local arrow_consumption = require("shared.systems.arrow-consumption")
local entity_types = require("shared.constants.entity-types")
local skill_types = require("shared.constants.skill-types")
local target_types = require("shared.constants.target-types")
local damage_types = require("shared.constants.damage-types")
local game_log = require("shared.lib.game-log")
local event_names = require("shared.constants.events")
local entity_name = require("shared.lib.entity-name")
local log_event_types = require("shared.constants.log-event-types")
local log_colors = require("shared.constants.log-colors")
local log_tags = require("shared.constants.log-tags")

local positional_check = require("shared.systems.positional-check")
local combat_rng = require("shared.systems.combat-rng")
local combat = require("shared.systems.combat")
local tp_formulas = require("shared.data.tp-formulas")
local combat_damage = require("shared.systems.combat-damage")
local offensive_interaction = require("shared.systems.offensive-interaction")

local M = {}

M.rng = combat_rng

local function shot_type_for_skill(skill)
  if skill.skill_type == skill_types.MAGIC_SKILL then
    return damage_types.MAGICAL
  end
  return damage_types.PHYSICAL
end

local function is_magical_formula(skill) return skill.skill_type == skill_types.MAGIC_SKILL end

M.shot_type_for_skill = shot_type_for_skill
M.is_magical_formula = is_magical_formula

function M.validate_completion(entity, skill_id, target)
  if entity.is_dead then
    return false
  end
  if entity.is_sleeping then
    return false
  end

  local skill = skills.get(skill_id)
  if not skill then
    return false
  end

  local skill_level = entity.known_skills and entity.known_skills[skill_id]
  if not skill_level then
    return false
  end

  local level_data = skills.get_level_data(skill_id, skill_level)
  if not level_data then
    return false
  end

  if skill.skill_type == skill_types.WEAPON_SKILL then
    if not entity.has_tp or not entity:has_tp(skill.tp_cost) then
      return false
    end
    if skill.weapon_skill_level_required and entity.get_weapon_skill_level then
      if entity:get_weapon_skill_level(skill.weapon_type) < skill.weapon_skill_level_required then
        return false
      end
    end
  else
    local already_deducted = entity.cast_initial_mp_deducted or 0
    local remaining_cost = (level_data.mp_cost or 0) - already_deducted
    if remaining_cost > 0 and entity.mp < remaining_cost then
      return false
    end
  end

  if skill.target_type == target_types.ENEMY then
    if not target or target.is_dead then
      return false
    end
    if target.network_kind == entity_types.PLAYER then
      return false
    end
    if entity.distance_to and level_data.range > 0 then
      if entity:distance_to(target) > skills.scale_range(level_data.range) then
        return false
      end
    end
  elseif skill.target_type == target_types.ALLY then
    if target and target.is_dead then
      return false
    end
    if target and entity.distance_to and level_data.range > 0 then
      if entity:distance_to(target) > skills.scale_range(level_data.range) then
        return false
      end
    end
  end

  return true, skill, level_data
end

function M.consume_shot_for_skill(entity, skill)
  if not entity.consume_active_shot then
    return
  end
  local shot_type = shot_type_for_skill(skill)
  entity:consume_active_shot(shot_type)
  if entity.load_shot then
    entity:load_shot(shot_type)
  end
end

function M.deduct_mp_and_set_cooldown(entity, skill, level_data)
  local already_deducted = entity.cast_initial_mp_deducted or 0
  local remaining_cost = (level_data.mp_cost or 0) - already_deducted
  if remaining_cost > 0 then
    entity.mp = entity.mp - remaining_cost
  end
  entity.cast_initial_mp_deducted = 0
  local recast = level_data.cooldown * (entity.recast_mod or 1)
  entity.action_cooldowns = entity.action_cooldowns or {}
  entity.action_cooldowns[skill.id] = recast
  entity.action_cooldown_totals = entity.action_cooldown_totals or {}
  entity.action_cooldown_totals[skill.id] = recast

  if skill.cooldown_group then
    for other_id, _ in pairs(entity.known_skills or {}) do
      if other_id ~= skill.id then
        local other = skills.get(other_id)
        if other and other.cooldown_group == skill.cooldown_group then
          entity.action_cooldowns[other_id] = recast
          entity.action_cooldown_totals[other_id] = recast
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

function M.build_skill_event(entity, skill, target)
  return combat.build_hit_event(event_names.SKILL_RESULT, entity, target, {
    skill_id = skill.id,
    element = skill.element,
    skill_type = skill.skill_type,
    skill_subtype = skill.skill_subtype,
  })
end

function M.log_skill(entity, recipient, skill, message, event_data)
  game_log.print(
    string.format(
      "[Skill] %s>%s: %s [%s] %s",
      entity.entity_type or "entity",
      recipient.entity_type or "entity",
      skill.display_name,
      skill.id,
      message
    ),
    log_colors.SKILL,
    event_data
  )
end

function M.calculate_skill_damage(entity, target, skill, level_data)
  local shot_type = shot_type_for_skill(skill)
  local multiplier = 1.0
  local soulshot_consumed = false
  if entity.consume_active_shot then
    local item = entity:consume_active_shot(shot_type)
    if item then
      multiplier = item.damage_multiplier
      soulshot_consumed = true
      logger.log(
        log_tags.COMBAT,
        { event = "shot_consumed", skill = skill.display_name, multiplier = multiplier }
      )
    end
  end

  local damage
  if not is_magical_formula(skill) then
    local wd = combat_damage.get_weapon_damage(entity)
      + combat_damage.get_weapon_skill_bonus(entity)
    local fstr = formulas.fSTR(entity.str or 0, target.con or 0, wd)
    local cR = formulas.combat_ratio(
      entity.p_atk * multiplier,
      target.p_def or 1,
      entity.level or 1,
      target.level or 1
    )
    local pdif = formulas.pDIF_roll(cR, M.rng.pdif_roll())
    damage = formulas.pdif_weapon_skill_damage(wd, fstr, level_data.power, pdif)
  else
    local element_bonus = 0
    if entity.m_atk_element and skill.element then
      element_bonus = entity.m_atk_element[skill.element] or 0
    end
    local m_atk_base = entity.m_atk
      + combat_damage.get_magic_skill_bonus(entity, skill.element)
      + element_bonus
    local fint = formulas.fINT(entity.int or 0, target.men or 0, m_atk_base)
    local mR = formulas.magic_ratio(
      m_atk_base * multiplier,
      target.m_def or 1,
      entity.level or 1,
      target.level or 1
    )
    local mdif = formulas.mDIF_roll(mR, M.rng.pdif_roll())
    damage = formulas.pdif_magical_damage(m_atk_base, fint, level_data.power, mdif)
  end
  if entity.skill_damage_mod and entity.skill_damage_mod[skill.id] then
    damage = damage * entity.skill_damage_mod[skill.id]
  end
  return math.max(1, damage), soulshot_consumed
end

function M.deal_damage(entity, target, damage)
  target.last_attacker = entity
  target:apply_damage(damage)
  offensive_interaction.apply(entity, target, damage)
end

function M.apply_spell_damage(entity, target, skill, level_data)
  local damage, _soulshot_consumed = M.calculate_skill_damage(entity, target, skill, level_data)
  M.deduct_mp_and_set_cooldown(entity, skill, level_data)
  M.deal_damage(entity, target, damage)
  M.log_skill(
    entity,
    target,
    skill,
    string.format("%d dmg (HP: %d/%d)", damage, target.hp, target.max_hp),
    {
      type = log_event_types.SKILL_HIT,
      source = entity_name(entity),
      target = entity_name(target),
      skill_name = skill.display_name,
      damage = damage,
    }
  )
  local event = M.build_skill_event(entity, skill, target)
  event.damage = damage
  if entity.load_shot then
    entity:load_shot(damage_types.MAGICAL)
  end
  if entity.try_magic_skillup and skill.element then
    local skilled_up = entity:try_magic_skillup(skill.element, combat_rng.pdif_roll())
    if skilled_up then
      event.magic_skill_up = {
        element = skill.element,
        new_level = entity:get_magic_skill_level(skill.element),
      }
    end
  end
  return event
end

function M.apply_weapon_skill_damage(entity, target, skill, level_data)
  local tp_spent = entity:consume_tp()
  local tp_multiplier = tp_formulas.tp_scaling_multiplier(tp_spent)

  local is_bow = arrow_consumption.has_bow_equipped(entity)
  local is_bow_skill = is_bow and not is_magical_formula(skill)
  if is_bow_skill and not arrow_consumption.try_consume(entity) then
    return nil
  end

  local positional_multiplier = 1.0
  local positional_zone = nil
  if skill.positional then
    local zones = skill.positional == "backstab" and positional_check.BACKSTAB_ZONES
      or positional_check.STANDARD_ZONES
    local zone_info = positional_check.get_zone(entity, target, zones)
    positional_multiplier = positional_check.get_multiplier(zone_info)
    positional_zone = zone_info.zone
  end

  local hits = skill.hit_count or 1
  local total_damage = 0
  local soulshot_consumed = false
  for i = 1, hits do
    if target.is_dead then
      break
    end
    local hit_damage, hit_soulshot = M.calculate_skill_damage(entity, target, skill, level_data)
    hit_damage = math.max(1, math.floor(hit_damage * positional_multiplier * tp_multiplier))
    M.deal_damage(entity, target, hit_damage)
    total_damage = total_damage + hit_damage
    if i == 1 then
      soulshot_consumed = hit_soulshot
    end
  end

  local zone_msg = positional_zone and string.format(" [%s zone]", positional_zone) or ""
  local hits_msg = hits > 1 and string.format(" (%dx)", hits) or ""
  M.log_skill(
    entity,
    target,
    skill,
    string.format(
      "%d dmg%s%s TP:%d (HP: %d/%d)",
      total_damage,
      hits_msg,
      zone_msg,
      tp_spent,
      target.hp,
      target.max_hp
    ),
    {
      type = log_event_types.SKILL_HIT,
      source = entity_name(entity),
      target = entity_name(target),
      skill_name = skill.display_name,
      damage = total_damage,
      hit_count = hits,
      zone = positional_zone,
      tp_spent = tp_spent,
    }
  )

  local event = M.build_skill_event(entity, skill, target)
  event.damage = total_damage
  event.hit_count = hits
  event.tp_spent = tp_spent
  if positional_zone then
    event.positional_zone = positional_zone
  end
  if is_bow_skill then
    event.arrow_hit = true
    event.soulshot = soulshot_consumed
  end
  if entity.load_shot then
    entity:load_shot(damage_types.PHYSICAL)
  end
  return event
end

return M
